brief: BofA's Global Rates Weekly argues the global bond selloff is driven mainly by Fed repricing, not just external shocks: resilient growth and elevated inflation keep pushing markets toward a higher peak fed funds rate, and cheap Treasury valuations plus weak auctions add a supply-demand component; BofA stays short 2y USTs and in 2s30s flatteners, and does not see rates as restrictive enough to end the move, though it says equities need 10y yields near 7% before valuations suffer materially. In Europe, higher energy-price and inflation forecasts push BofA's economists to add a December ECB hike to their base case, delaying euro curve steepening to 2027; UK BoE is now expected to hike in November and February to 4.25%, helped by contained August public finances. In Australia, BofA rotates its RBA OIS paid position from September to November and expects a hawkish hike; in Japan, foreign investors keep favoring JGB curve flatteners against the global steepener consensus, with no evidence GPIF has increased its JGB allocation.
